differences.what: T-2221: the two Prairie corners now have framed receiver heads, narrow necks, continuous wall-offset leaders and broad straps. The north head close-up was reviewed on the final canonical web asset; raised framing is readable under the bounded matte finish. Exact small casting ornament, stock dimensions and hidden connections remain reconstructed.

T-2222: the middle and south stacks expose substantially longer shafts below the main ridge than Taylor shows. Their footprint positions retained the earlier ridge datum and require independent early-photo/elevation reconciliation.

T-2228: whole-house masonry relief/coursing and tone, window profiles and placement, roof/coping silhouette and absolute eave/head placement still differ. The five-control camera is fitted to current house geometry, not an independent survey; no exact photographic match is claimed.
The monochrome early photograph cannot establish the July 1904 rainwater colour, unseen court runs or concealed sockets. Reconstructed grey-green finish is not a sampled historical colour.
The isolated-building comparison omits the street, planted trees and adjoining Keith house. The far-left ornate tower belongs to that neighboring parcel, not to Glessner.

T-2222: the unchanged early Taylor camera now shows middle and south shafts near the ridge with short exposed fronts and flush masonry cap courses, replacing the overly long roof-front projections. North-gable top, stack count and roof geometry remain unchanged. Cap joints and flue depths remain bounded reconstruction; existing whole-house differences are not resolved by this component review.
